memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "God also said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.' This is my name forever, the name you shall call me from generation to generation."" - Exodus 3:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God ties His eternal name to three specific men — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob. He is not an abstract philosophical idea. He is a God with a history, who made promises to real people and kept them.

Then He adds: this is my name forever, from generation to generation.

There is something deeply reassuring here for families. The God your grandmother prayed to is the same God available to your children. Faith is not a private discovery each generation must make from scratch. It is a testimony handed down.

But it must be handed down deliberately. In the book of Judges we read the tragic line that a generation grew up who did not know the Lord. Faith is never automatically inherited.

So tell the stories. Tell your children and grandchildren what God has done in your life — the prayers answered, the provisions given, the times He held you. Paul reminded Timothy of the faith that first lived in his grandmother and mother (2 Tim 1:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done in my life that I have never told the next generation?
2. Whose faith was passed to me, and have I thanked God for them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for those who passed the faith to me. Help me to speak of Your goodness so the next generation knows Your name. Amen.
